digest.component_or_area: RP-04 architecture secrets and authentication design
propositions: Rebar must safely support multiple LLM, CI, repository, and issue-tracking providers across diverse deployment environments without weakening SDK-native refresh, workload identity, credential helpers, rotation, or redaction.

Operation snapshots must remain structurally non-secret; provider-native credential and session capabilities are injected into Rebar-owned factories; static credentials use provider-specific non-serializable SecretStr/SecretBytes containers and are unwrapped only at the sending adapter.

Static credential rotation in long-running processes requires restart or redeploy; native temporary credentials owned by upstream SDKs may refresh in-process; Rebar does not poll environment, retrieve secrets at runtime, watch files, or maintain hot-reload caches.

Deployment resolves external secret stores (SSM, files, environment) before process startup; Rebar accepts REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH (preferred) or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY; no application-owned SSM retrieval, universal secret broker, or built-in cloud-secret manager is introduced.

Trusted same-capability child subprocesses inherit ambient environment; Rebar never mutates global os.environ to install secrets; static credentials overlay only onto owning children; unrelated siblings remove only exact Rebar-declared secret variable names; deployment step/container/service scoping is the primary security boundary.
